hook.text: 'I goed to the store.' 'She runned fast.' Children make errors that prove they've learned the rule.

buildup.text: Overgeneralization means applying a regular rule to irregular forms—adding '-ed' to all past tenses.

discovery.text: Children first say 'went' correctly (memorized), then switch to 'goed' once they learn the '-ed' rule.

twist.text: This U-shaped learning curve shows that getting worse temporarily means deeper learning is happening.

climax.text: Overgeneralization errors are evidence that children are rule-learners, not just imitators.

punchline.text: Errors can be proof of progress—rules overshoot before settling.

quiz.question: What does overgeneralization suggest about children?
options: They are actively learning rules, not just imitating
